children: Sky Protocol, a decentralized finance platform, saw more than $2 billion of stablecoin redemptions in a single day after allegations surfaced that it had processed illicit funds.

Cointelegraph reported on Nov. 20 that more than $2 billion of USDS was exchanged the previous day for Circle's dollar-backed stablecoin USDC. The transactions were carried out through the Peg Stability Module, or PSM, which is designed to allow the two stablecoins to be swapped at a fixed ratio.

The heavy redemptions came shortly after a report said some transactions routed through Sky Protocol were tied to illicit funds. CoinDesk reported on Nov. 19, citing an investigation by blockchain analytics firm Inca Digital, that about $518 million of transactions over the past five years had been processed through Sky Protocol from wallets linked to high-risk actors, including hackers and sanctioned entities.

Of that amount, about $101.9 million was assessed as linked to North Korea-related hacking groups. The transactions included wallets connected to the Bybit hack in February 2025. The report raised concerns in the market that user redemptions could be restricted if Circle, the issuer of USDC, were to freeze assets held by Sky Protocol.

Sky Protocol rejected the allegations and said the system functioned smoothly despite the surge in redemptions. In a statement released on Nov. 20, it said USDS held at $1 even during the period of heaviest redemption demand, and that USDC holdings in the PSM never fell below $800 million. The balance had recovered to more than $1.1 billion as of Nov. 20.

Block Analitica, a risk-management adviser to the Sky ecosystem, also disputed CoinDesk's analysis. It said the $518 million in flagged transactions accounted for less than 0.06% of the $960 billion in cumulative volume processed through Sky's Peg Stability Module.

It added that about two-thirds of the suspicious transactions occurred between 2021 and mid-2024, before the introduction of a new exchange system called LitePSM. Some addresses classified as North Korea-linked wallets may also have been only indirectly connected, several transaction steps removed from wallets that were actually under sanctions.

The redemption wave reduced USDS circulation by about 40% in a day to roughly 3.2 billion tokens. Even with the sharp supply contraction, USDS maintained its dollar peg. CoinDesk said wallets linked to crypto exchange Poloniex accounted for a large share of the redeemed amount, though it was not confirmed whether the exchange itself carried out the redemptions.

Sky Protocol also emphasized that its reserve assets exceed the amount of stablecoins in circulation. According to its treasury data, the combined circulating supply of USDS and DAI stood at about $6.11 billion as of Nov. 20, while backing assets totaled about $9.3 billion. It also held a separate reserve fund of about $93 million against potential losses.

title: Sky Protocol Faces $2 Billion in Redemptions Amid Illicit-Funds Claims; USDS Holds Peg
